On 30 November 2021, around 10 climate activists belonging to Insulate Britain gathered outside Downing Street in London - Westminster to urge the government to fund the insulation of homes in the country as a way to reduce carbon dioxide emissions and combat climate change. Protesters staged a hunger strike, demanding the release of two protesters who were arrested following earlier protests organised by Insulate Britain in which they blocked motorways and roads as part of the protest.

On 25 September 2023, climate activists staged a protest outside the Crown Court in London - Westminster (England) against the decision by the Attorney General's Office to prosecute fellow activist Trudi Warner. She was arrested in March after allegedly communicating to jurors with a sign during the trial of Insulate Britain protesters. The event was part of a national day of action.

On 4 June 2024, at the call of CR, around 60 farmers gathered outside the gendarmerie station in Auch (Occitanie) to express solidarity with Lionel Candelon, head of the departmental CR branch, who was arrested and interrogated for a protest action on 27 May, where he damaged the French Biodiversity Office (OFB) building. The protesters also called for a dissolution of the OFB.

On 24 February 2022, around 70 people, who were majority women, waving pro-feminist and anti-police banners rallied outside Newport Central Police Station in Newport in support of Jennifer Swain, who was arrested for placing stickers around the city. Protesters demanded women's rights, women's safety, police support for women, rape, and gender identity. A Swansea University student spoke at the protest, while Merched Cymru, Women's Rights, and the Lesbian Labour group members attended the rally.

On 8 May 2022, Amnesty International activists gathered in Altamura (Bari, Puglia) to protest against the repression of dissent in Russia, where over 15,000 people demonstrating against the war in Ukraine were allegedly arrested.

On 27 October 2024, climate and environmental activists, including from Ethical Alliance (Alliance ethique) and SSCS, gathered outside the Japan Matsuri fair in Montpellier (Occitanie) to demand the release of Paul Watson, the founder of Sea Shepherd and a prominent defender of marine ecosystems. Watson was arrested in Greenland on 21 July 2024, while heading toward a Japanese harpoon vessel. The demonstrators protested against his potential extradition to Japan and advocated for his continued fight to protect marine life and the environment.

On 24 September 2022, a group of people protested in the city center in Hamburg - Hamburg-Mitte (Hamburg) to demonstrate against the systemic rule and discrimination against women in Iran. One headscarf was burned at the protest and several people symbolically cut their hair off to protest. The current protests were triggered by the death of a woman who was arrested by the morality police for infringing hijab rules.

On 5 December 2020, demonstrators gathered in Macon, on the Lamartine quay, at the call of local organizations. They denounced financial precariousness and called for the removal of article 24 of the 'comprehensive security' bill and denounced its potential infringement of the principle of freedom of information, especially on reporting on police brutality. The article criminalizes disseminating images with personal identifiers of a police or military officer, with the aim of affecting his or her physical or psychological integrity.

On 11 June 2020, at night, around 50 police officers gathered at the Stanislas place in Nancy and dropped their handcuffs on the floor. They protested against the declarations of the Minister of the Interior about implementing changes in the police arrest techniques that were made in response to a row of protests in the country against racism and police brutality.

On 5 December 2020, around 100 people, including many Yellow Vests, gathered on Place de la Bourse in Bordeaux (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to protest against police violence. Later that afternoon, around 200 people, at the call of CGT, LDH, and other unions, rallied on Place de la Victoire to denounce layoffs, unemployment, and financial precariousness. The two groups joined together into a single march that grew to nearly 1,000 participants before dispersing around 4:30 pm without clashes, under a prefectural order barring demonstrators from entering central shopping streets.
